lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: First Hawaiian (FHB), BOH's only same-market peer, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-23. Its margin rose 5bp to 3.30%, above its own Q2-call outlook of about 3.27%. Its interest-bearing deposit cost FELL 3bp to 1.72% even though the Fed hiked mid-quarter, and total deposits grew $50M to $20.2B, so Hawaii deposit pricing did not reprice up after the hike. BOH guided about +5bp a quarter (2.78% to about 2.83-2.84%) with deposit costs of 1.25-1.30%; if FHB's pattern carries over, BOH's Q3 margin and net interest income land at the top of that path or above it.

findings.finding: FHB took a $20.3M provision in Q3 (Q2: $5.6M), driven by a $12.5M partial charge-off on a single CRE loan plus other CRE downgrades. Net charge-offs were 0.60% annualized (Q2: 0.11%) and nonperforming assets rose to $46.0M from $39.5M. BOH's own criticized assets rose to 2.81% from 2.12% in Q2 because of one borrower (93% real-estate secured, about 58% weighted LTV). A charge-off or migration on that BOH credit in Q3 would cost provision against a consensus that assumes about $3-4M.

findings.finding: Two hurricanes hit Hawaii in Q3. Lala (2026-08-14) closed BOH branches on Hawai'i Island and Maui; Lowell (2026-09-07/08) closed all BOH branches on Kaua'i. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior BOH print that turned on a weather event in the baseline window. The April 2026 Kona-low storms preceded a -0.04% reaction (2026-04-20).
